title: Martial arts of Europe, Africa and the Americas
blurb: The wrestling and swordplay Europe wrote down in manuals, the stick and fist sports of Africa and Egypt, and the ring sports the Americas made out of both — up to the cage.

items.s: Boxing is a combat sport and martial art.
Bare-knuckle boxing (also known as bare-knuckle or bare-knuckle fighting) is a full-contact combat sport based on punching without any form of padding on the hands.
Greco-Roman (American English) (spelled Graeco- or Græco- in British English) or classic wrestling (European English) is a style of wrestling that is practiced worldwide.
Freestyle wrestling is a style of wrestling.
Catch wrestling (also known as catch-as-catch-can) is an English wrestling style with fewer restrictions than other wrestling styles.
Fencing is a combat sport that features sword fighting.
Historical European martial arts (HEMA) are martial arts of European origin, particularly using arts formerly practised, but having since died out or evolved into very different forms.
The German school of fencing (Deutsche Schule; Kunst des Fechtens) is a system of combat taught in the Holy Roman Empire during the Late Medieval, German Renaissance, and early modern periods.

Ringen is the German language term for grappling (wrestling).

Dambe is a martial art of the Hausa people from Nigeria.
